steps.title: Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have your joints felt since you finished care with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still feeling good, some pain returning, or pretty much back to where you started. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Feeling Good
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes care with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Pain Starting to Return
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Joint pain can return after care ends. Your notes say you had made good progress. What do you think brought it back?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Pain Fully Back
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Joint pain can return after care ends. Your notes say you had made good progress. Was there a new injury, or did it return slowly?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask a few questions about your joints?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to {{complaint_reference}}. First, can I ask a few joint questions so your file is current?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Joint Questions
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Is either knee bothering you?

How about either hip?

Is either shoulder bothering you?

Any trouble with your hands or grip?

Any neck or back pain?

Any morning stiffness?

Any swelling after activity?

Are you taking any medications for joint pain?

Of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Joint Questions
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Is either knee bothering you?

How about either hip?

Is either shoulder bothering you?

Any trouble with your hands or grip?

Any neck or back pain?

Any morning stiffness?

Any swelling after activity?

Are you taking any medications for joint pain?

Between these and what returned, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Understand the Concern
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask about {{main_concern}} so your file is current.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} has been bothering you. I don't want to assume anything. Is it timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Let them answer. Do not argue.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad your joints are still feeling good.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in for check-ins?

(Let them answer. Do not argue.)

(Tap the reason they shared.)

steps.title: Objection: Pain Returned
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me, {{contact_first_name}}. That's one of the most common reasons people call us back.

How long after you stopped did you notice it again?

(Let them answer.)

When a joint flares back up that soon, it usually means it was calmer but not fully settled. Care stopped a little early, or you got back to using it harder than expected. Either way, you're not back at square one. You already did the hard part once.

We'd rather have {{provider_name}} check it now than let it stiffen up again. You'll hear where things stand and what it would take.

Can we get you in for a look?

steps.title: Objection: Getting Older
steps.content:
I hear that a lot, {{contact_first_name}}, and I understand why.

Can I ask, is it the same joint as before, or is it showing up in new places now?

(Let them answer.)

Age is part of it, but it isn't the whole story. Plenty of people your age aren't dealing with {{main_concern}}. Usually the joint is being loaded unevenly, and that part can be changed. Writing it off as age means living with it when you might not have to.

A visit with {{provider_name}} sorts out which part is age and which part we can help with. If it really is just wear, we'll tell you that.

Wouldn't you rather know which one it is?

steps.title: Objection: Pain Relievers
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. A lot of people get by that way.

How often are you reaching for them now compared to a few months ago?

(Let them answer. Do not comment on their medication.)

If it's creeping up, that tells you something. The pills quiet the pain, but they don't change what the joint is doing. So the pain is right back the moment they wear off. Covering something and fixing it are two different things.

A check with {{provider_name}} tells you which one you're dealing with. If what you're taking is enough, we'll say so. If it isn't, you'll find out now instead of a year from now.

Would it help to know for sure?

steps.title: Reason: Feeling Fine
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When your joints feel good, coming in stops feeling urgent. Check-ins help us notice changes before they disrupt your routine.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a joint check-in on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. You're not committing to treatment. The first step is a visit to check how your joints are doing.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get that joint check-in scheduled. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Life Got Busy
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and check-ins get pushed down the list. We can find a time that works around your schedule.

Would that help?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's find an easy time for a joint check-in. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Waiting for Pain
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Joint changes can begin before they interfere with your day. A check-in lets us see how things are holding up.

Would a quick check-in work?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a joint check-in on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Reason: Moved or Switched
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're nearby, your joint care history is still in your file here.

Would you like us to take another look?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap it. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a joint check-in on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to {{complaint_reference}}. First, can I ask a few joint questions so your file is current?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Joint Questions
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Is either knee bothering you?

How about either hip?

Is either shoulder bothering you?

Any trouble with your hands or grip?

Any neck or back pain?

Any morning stiffness?

Any swelling after activity?

Are you taking any medications for joint pain?

Between these and the pain that's back, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like physical therapy, injections, or another office?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all help, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what's going on with {{main_concern}} right now. {{provider_name}} already knows your history and how you responded last time, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it more the cost of the visit itself, or not knowing what insurance will cover?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Insurance changes every year, so a lot of people aren't sure what they have now. Our front desk can check your coverage before you come in, so there are no surprises. And this first visit is one appointment, not a plan. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first visit, or the worry about coming in a lot like before?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that's a handful of visits to settle it down. Sometimes it's more, and you'll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is signing you up for a long plan on the phone.

We have early and late openings. Since you've been here before, the first visit is usually under 30 minutes.

Could you find half an hour for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that it hurts and you don't know why. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: Needs Time
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} has been going on for a while now. It's had time to sort itself out on its own, and it hasn't. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: Send Information
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you why {{main_concern}} keeps flaring up for you. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at you, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
